text:
India on Tuesday expressed deep concern about the situation in West Asia and backed efforts to restore peace and ensure the smooth flow of trade as external affairs minister S Jaishankar met his UAE counterpart Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Mumbai to review bilateral ties.
Sheikh Abdullah, who arrived in the financial hub on Monday, said the UAE is keen to do more to bolster cooperation in areas ranging from trade to people-to-people ties. The UAE is currently India’s third largest trading partner after China and the US, and two-way trade is worth more than $100 billion.
“The situation in the Gulf remains a matter of deep concern. We will continue to work together and support all efforts to promote dialogue and diplomacy,” Jaishankar said at the start of his meeting with Sheikh Abdullah.
“We continue to support free, safe and unimpeded flow of trade, energy and fertilisers. I would also like to thank you today, and through you, the UAE leadership, for ensuring the well-being of the Indian community in the UAE,” he said, referring to the presence of some 4.5 million Indians in the Emirates.
The India-UAE economic partnership continues to set new benchmarks despite global headwinds and regional challenges, with bilateral trade surpassing $100 billion since the two sides signed the comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) in 2022, Jaishankar said. Two-way investments have continued to grow, reflecting businesses’ confidence in each other’s economies, while cooperation in defence, energy and technology is “acquiring a strategic character”, he said.
Sheikh Abdullah, the latest in a string of senior Emirati leaders to visit India as the two sides worked to shore up their relations amid the uncertainty created by the West Asia conflict, said his country wanted to further enhance bilateral cooperation.
The UAE is honoured to be one of India’s largest trading partners, and the Emirati leadership aims for a closer, stronger, and more diverse relationship, he said.
“We are very close but we want to be closer,” Sheikh Abdullah said. The UAE wants to do more with India in areas such as people-to-people ties, culture and education, he said.
Jaishankar subsequently said on social media that he had a productive meeting with Sheikh Abdullah, who is also deputy prime minister of the UAE, and two sides undertook a comprehensive review of their ties.
“The breadth and ambition of our cooperation is visible across the domains of trade, investments, energy, technology, logistics, defence, education and people-to-people ties,” he said in the social media post.
The two sides have had several high-level engagements this year. UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed visited India in January, while Sheikh Khalid, the crown prince of Abu Dhabi, led the UAE delegation to the AI Impact Summit in February and the Brics Summit in September. Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the UAE in May.
Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. Read More
